messages.text: I can pull that up for you. What's the email address you used when you placed the order? It's the one your confirmation came to. I'll use it to match Shop···· and give you the ship date.

Found it. Your order is paid and hasn't shipped yet. Both the B30 and the Power Kit are still waiting to go out.

The B30 is a pre-sale unit and ships October 30. I'm sorry, I know you were looking at an earlier date than that.

We'll send the delivery notices to (email hidden) automatically. It's worth whitelisting us so the tracking email doesn't end up in spam.

<details><summary>Note for you (not shown to the customer)</summary>

The order's own date for the B30 is September 5, 2026, which has already passed. So under the late rules this counts as a late order, not an on-time one. I gave the October 30 date because the product facts say it overrides the date on the order. That fact says "Harlo B30", but this line is titled "BSB B30" (sku `bsbb30`). I took them to be the same unit, and nothing in the lookup confirms it.

I couldn't check whether we'd already written to this customer about the delay. The instructions point to a `comms_history.py` script that isn't in the skill folders. So the reply apologises for the later date but doesn't say whether we told them before. The lookup gives no name, so I didn't use one. It also has no date for the Power Kit, so I only said it's still to ship.

The customer only asked for a status, so I didn't offer a credit, swap or refund, and I didn't flag it. The September 5 date is less than 3 weeks past as of the latest guidance (September 24). If the customer isn't happy with the new date, the next step is the credit and retention options.

</details>
Can I still seek a refund since the order has not shipped?

Yes, you can. The order hasn't shipped, so it can still be cancelled and refunded. It's a pre-sale order, so cancelling it carries a 10% restocking fee. Keeping the order costs you nothing extra.

Before we go that way, can I ask what changed? Is it the move to October 30, or something else? The B30 is still the best value per TH in our lineup, so if it's the wait, there may be something I can do to make that easier.

<details><summary>Note for you (not shown to the customer)</summary>

I told the customer about the 10% fee now, although the playbook saves it for the last attempt. They asked directly whether they can get a refund, and the fee changes what they get back. I didn't quote an amount because they paid $851.03 for the B30 and Power Kit together, not the $899 list price. I don't know what the B30 line alone cost.

This delay is on our side. A fee on a refund for a late order is likely to cause pushback. The rules still apply the fee to pre-sale orders, so I didn't waive it. If they object, a person should decide.

I haven't offered the $50 credit or flagged anything yet. Next step: if they're unhappy about the wait, I'll offer the $50. If they still want the refund, I'll flag it as refund_request so Abel or Georges can process it.

</details>
